title: Annotatio IV §.VI cont.: Irenaeus (3–4) — two things of the Eucharist; celestial = supernatural presence mode
pass_a_gloss: (3) judging that the Sacred Eucharist, not the bread, consists of two things, lest anyone think Christ’s body is joined with the bread even outside the lawful use of the Eucharist. (4) calling one of the two things earthly, namely bread born from the earth, but the other heavenly — and thus not Christ’s body naturally or corporally present, which body itself as a heavenly thing, unless by Manichaean Heresy, according to the Holy Spirit’s true mind ought to be held an entirely earthly thing, formed from Mary’s bloody mass … most like us and our Infants in all things even as to local presence, sin alone excepted — But called heavenly on account of the solely heavenly and supernatural mode of presence in the Eucharist, genuine food of our faithful souls born from heaven, nay from the Holy Spirit, hereafter to have most wholesome use even in the bodies of the faithful, i.e. to procure their blessed resurrection unto eternal life.
pass_b_english: (3) The two things belong to the Eucharist, not to the bread alone — lest Christ’s body be joined to bread even outside lawful use. (4) Earthly = bread from earth; heavenly is not Christ’s body naturally/corporally present (that body is an earthly thing from Mary’s mass, like us except sin).
It is called heavenly for the solely supernatural presence-mode in the Eucharist — genuine food of faithful souls from the Spirit, someday serving even their bodies toward blessed resurrection.
source_text: (3) Eucharistiam S., non verò panem, ex duabus rebus censere constare, ne quis cum pane, etiam extra usum Eucharistiæ legitimum, corpus Christi conjungi arbitretur. (4) Duarum rerum alteram, terrenam vocitare, scil. panem è terra natum, alteram verò cælestem, eòque non corpus Christi naturaliter seu corporaliter præsens, quod ipsum corpus res cælestis, non nisi per Hæresin Manichaicam, juxta Spiritûs S. verò mentem, res omnino terrena haberi debet, ex Massa Mariæ sanguinea formata, in utero ejusdem concepta, fota, nutrita, definitô tempore, ex utero materno in mundi lucem egressa, nobis & nostris Infantibus per omnia, etiam ratione præsentiæ localis, unico exceptô peccatô, simillima, Sed verò ob cœlestem unicè ac supernaturalem in Eucharistia præsentiæ modum, cælestis dicta, animarum nostrarum fidelium, eatenus ex cœlo, quin ex Spiritu S. natarum, genuinum pabulum, etiam in corporibus fidelium, saluberrimum usum olim habiturum, i. e. horum beatam ad vitam æternam, procuraturum resurrectionem.
